inputs.original_text: Taoiseach Micheál Martin said in Limerick this past week that housing tenancies have increased, despite concerns about rising eviction notices and homelessness following new Government rules introduced on March 1 requiring landlords to provide tenants with six-year leases. The number of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again.
inputs.modified_text: Micheál Martin’s claim in Limerick that housing tenancies have increased sounds like carefully chosen cover: point to one reassuring figure while people face rising eviction notices and homelessness under the rules introduced on March 1. Those rules require landlords to provide six-year leases, yet emergency accommodation numbers increased again nationally. The contrast looks less like reassurance than an effort to manage the story while the damage continues.
